concept: One comment, one meeting. A single chat bubble over the same cartoon meeting room changes state part by part: vague and warm, then behaviour, then effect, then one step. The viewer watches the same object get fixed, tries a faded version on Dev's call, then sees the opening frame return changed: next week Sam lets Priya finish.

devices.what: THE comment: one chat bubble whose contents swap in place. Vague words in grey, then each part arrives in its own calm tint, the earlier version fading to a ghost behind it. Text lives on this object.
The same meeting room cutaway (Sam, Priya, the manager, two muted background colleagues), its state changed: emptying, a week later, replayed, next week in full colour.

Three slot objects: behaviour (accent3), effect (field2), one step (accent4). They open at the end of the bubble, lift off as tiles, reappear on the answer cards, the sticky note and beside the presenter.

Stepped time: a small wall calendar in the meeting room flips one page, next week, and the room is re-staged in one step. The failure in the hook (carried by the b02 time join) and the success in the payoff.
Answer cards with three tick discs (observable, real effect, one step). Ticks drop on their words; a missing tick stays an empty dashed disc.
The one join material: a page turn of the paper ground at section boundaries (b06, b13, b16); inside a topic the comment bubble carries across (continue, handoff).

parts.what: The meeting room set: Loom.place.meeting cutaway with a long table (near face field2), surface2 wall, a window, a door, chairs in muted (never accent), a small wall calendar on the left wall. Room is slightly desaturated until state next_week_full. Named people are placed by the scene as peep busts behind the table edge (not part of the kit).

The comment: a chat-style bubble (seed bubble chat, round shape, ink outline, surface fill) with a soft tail, Nunito body text. Holds up to three part slots in a row of lines: behaviour (accent3 tint), effect (field2 tint), one step (accent4 tint). The newest part carries an accent underline; settled parts keep their tint only. A ghost layer shows the previous wording at 15 % opacity behind. Vague state reads: Great energy in there today (muted ink on cream).

A small paper wall calendar with an accent3 header band; its page flips once in stepped time (two drawings, no tween) from this week to next week, with the hand-lettered words Next week on the new page.

design.treatment: A wide frame split into two balanced halves. Left half (x 120 to 860): a small video-call tile with Dev's cartoon figure and an empty agenda slot (a dashed outline labelled 'Agenda' with nothing in it), kicker 'Now you' above and the question line below it. Right half (x 980 to 1800): three equal answer cards, same width (820) and height (150), in ONE vertical column, evenly spaced 40 px apart and vertically centred on the frame, each with its letter disc (A, B, C) and its text. No card is marked or favoured. A small pause ring with 'Pause and decide' settles under the column at the end.
design.why_motion: Each card slides in from the right on its own spoken letter so the learner hears and reads each option once, as peers; the column then rests through the pause.

scenes.rationale: The allocation fixes this beat as an avatar. Avatar props are only title, kicker and a card of up to 3 lines, with no focus or zoom, so the storyboard has no setting that moves the card off the left of the plate. I tried switching to the recap template and the gate rejected it (allocation says avatar). The empty right panel is most likely the presenter slot rendering without a presenter. This is reported to the engine route and not verified. The recap alternative is ready so a switch is one step if the allocation changes.
